messages:
tara: heads up — customer (acct:redwood-corp) opened a support ticket: Dedicated dashboard for ded-nyc-03 shows 8 GPUs but nodes report 12 after we changed node labels.
kevin: which change/when? can you paste the cluster id and exact command you ran? :eyes:
tara: cluster_id: ded-nyc-03. Change happened ~2025-09-12T17:24Z. We applied a label update to standardize gpu-type names:
```
kubectl label nodes -l pool=dedicated env=prod gpu-type=gpu-v2 --overwrite
```
sam: looking at metrics pipeline (prom -> metrics-store -> inventory-service). Prometheus query `sum(node_gpu_count{cluster="ded-nyc-03"})` returns 12 for 17:25Z, so node exporters are fine.
maria: dashboard backing source is the inventory materialized view (inventory_snapshots). That table was last refreshed at 17:00Z and refresh interval is 1h. If indexer failed during the label change, snapshot could be stale.
infra-bot: deploy event: ded-inventory-indexer v2.3 deployed by @kevin at 2025-09-12T17:23:12Z
kevin: I pushed a small parser change for label keys right before the label rollout. Did the indexer crash? logs?
maria: checked indexer logs, saw repeated errors right after 17:24Z. snippet:
```
ERROR parsing node labels for node ip-10-2-3-14: unknown label value "gpu-v2": cannot coerce
panic: failed to process node update
```
sam: that would make the indexer drop the node entry and it wouldn't appear in the snapshot. Inventory service returns lower counts until snapshot refresh.
tara: customer timeline: they saw drop at 17:27Z and raised ticket CR-2371.
kevin: I'll restart the indexer pod and tail logs. `kubectl -n infra rollout restart deployment/ded-inventory-indexer` — doing now.
kevin: restarted, watching logs... indexer is now up and processing backlog; I see it reconciling 4 missing nodes.
maria: because snapshot cadence is hourly, dashboard won't show fixes until snapshot refresh. I can trigger a manual refresh: `CALL refresh_inventory_snapshots('ded-nyc-03');`
maria: ran manual refresh at 17:48Z.
tara: dashboard now shows 12 GPUs. customer confirmed in ticket: thanks for quick fix.
sam: root cause categorization: (1) label parsing bug in indexer caused node entries to be skipped; (2) inventory materialized snapshots run hourly so UI showed stale data for up to 1h.
kevin: mitigation actions: PR #412 fixes label parsing (adding backward-compatible parsing), hotfix applied to indexer; reduce snapshot refresh from 60m -> 5m for Dedicated clusters; add cache invalidation webhook on node label patch to trigger immediate refresh for affected cluster.
tara: I'll draft a short customer-facing note and update the internal postmortem. Assigning follow-ups: KEVIN -> merge hotfix and deploy to prod; MARIA -> change snapshot cadence and add monitoring; SAM -> add a dashboard alert for inventory-snapshot lag.
support-bot: ticket CR-2371 updated: dashboard counts corrected, customer notified. status: resolved (pending postmortem).
kevin: added runbook entry: "If Dedicated dashboard shows discrepancy after node label changes" with commands and query. link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/inventory-discrepancy
maria: added a unit test for label parsing and a CI check for snapshots failing to refresh.
tara: closing loop with customer and tagging for postmortem. good job team :thumbsup!
kevin: recommend we add an end-to-end smoke test for Dedicated inventory after infra changes (terraform/k8s labels) to catch this in pre-prod.
sam: agreed. I'll open the follow-up tickets.
infra-bot: note: ded-inventory-indexer pod restart by @kevin at 2025-09-12T17:42:11Z logged.
support-bot: CR-2371: customer message added — "Dashboard correct now, thanks. Please confirm what happened and how to avoid."
